# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). A uv workspace of four packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (index row count × request rate; not yet measured); measured by Stage 2 |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk; measured by Stage 3 |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index files into one table
      Objective: Build one filing-index table from real quarterly and daily master index files.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: the four-package uv workspace scaffold; nothing from prior stages
      Produces: a filing-index table on disk built from real quarterly and daily indexes; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — a query over the table returns the rows of at least one real quarterly index and one real daily index; the findings file records the real run's wall time, bytes downloaded, request count, row count and peak memory
      Leaves out: manifests, traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submissions downloaded
      Objective: Download the submissions that the filing-index table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: the submissions for the range set in the stage session, on disk; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by the table's rows within that range is on disk, or is listed as not downloaded; the findings file records the measured download rate, bytes and file count, and the projected cost of the full history
      Leaves out: manifests, traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick the 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk
      Produces: the extracted main documents of the 10-K and 8-K filings in those submissions; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-3-findings.md
      Exit: O3 — each 10-K and 8-K submission on disk has its main document extracted to a file, or is listed with the reason it was not; the findings file records the run's wall time, volume and failure count
      Leaves out: manifests, traceability (Stage 4); point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Add manifests and traceability across the index table, the submissions and the extracted documents.
      Outcomes: none new; hardens O1–O3 with manifests, traceability
      Consumes: Stages 1–3's outputs
      Produces: a manifest of every source file and output, with each output traceable to the source bytes it came from
      Exit: manifests — a rerun after an interruption resumes from the manifest without repeating completed files; traceability — any table row, submission or extracted document resolves to its source URL and content hash
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness (Stage 5); full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Make the filing-index table point-in-time aware, so that later corrections to quarterly indexes are reconciled without losing earlier source history.
      Outcomes: none new; hardens O1 (and what O2 reads from it) with point-in-time awareness
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifests and source hashes
      Produces: a filing-index table that records additions, changes and withdrawals per source snapshot
      Exit: point-in-time awareness — re-reading a changed quarterly index records its differences, and the table as of an earlier snapshot can still be read
      Leaves out: full validation suites (Stage 6); scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suites
      Objective: Cover the index, submission and extraction layers with full validation suites on committed fixtures.
      Outcomes: none new; hardens O1–O3 with full validation suites
      Consumes: Stages 1–5's outputs
      Produces: a fixture-based suite that runs in CI without SEC access
      Exit: full validation suites — CI passes on committed fixtures, malformed and legacy formats included, with no request to the SEC
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Deploy the ingestion and schedule its ongoing daily and reconciliation runs.
      Outcomes: none new; hardens O1–O3 with scheduling and deployment
      Consumes: Stages 4–6's outputs
      Produces: a deployed environment that runs the ingestion on a schedule
      Exit: scheduling and deployment — an observed scheduled daily run extends the filing-index table with no manual step, and its report is retained
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
